posts.cooked:
Had a great game against advanced Voss tonight. Tachyon, Haka, Bunker, and the Wraith. Wraith used her infrared eyepiece to hold off Forced Deployments until the villain trash was full to bursting. Finally, one of them hit the table. On Tachyon’s turn she destroyed the Forced Deployment. Sixteen minions marched dutifully onto the table, and Haka Rampaged them all to death instantly. My group still hasn’t beaten Dawn yet, though…

posts.name: arenson9
posts.cooked:
TheJayManm, Rabit, me, and five of our friends got together to play Sentinels today. We played eight total games. It might have been more if four of us didn’t end up in a very slow (fun, but S L O W) whittling of Citizen Dawn. Totally stoked to actually beat her after losing most of our hit points before doing virtually any damage to her. Three quarters of the team would have qualified for Last Man Standing. Playing the Wraith vs Dawn on Mars == lots of equipment loss.

One of the best parts of the day was facing Omnitron on standard mode and attempting to get a Flawless Victory. With both police backups as well as Bunker doing 2 pts of damage each turn, we actually contemplated trying to find a way to heal Omnitron to give us more time to heal ourselves. In the end, Omnitron got out both of the one-shots that cleared equipment and ongoing cards as well as doing a ton of damage. The heroes then realized it was time to stop show-boating and finish him off. We did, at least, let The Real Heroes do the destroying.

posts.cooked:
This isn’t really about points, but two nights ago, we had our biggest success: we finally beat Matriarch and Chairman, in one night. It was amazing. I don’t wanna go into every detail, so basically:

Chairman was still really hard, and we would have lost if Tony Taurus hadn’t been there to stop a jailbreak which would have freed all of the underbosses.

Matriarch was… easy. I’m not kidding: we had the most incredible luck I’ve ever seen. She didn’t even flip! You know how usually she’ll get these long chains where like 10 fowls will come into play in one turn? She hardly got any chains at all. I think her biggest chain was 3 fowls. It was uncanny. I’m sad it wasn’t very nail-bitingly tense, which I like my games to be, but after the multiple times in the past where she utterly destroyed us, it felt good to turn it around and just destroy her.

posts.name: pcgamerpirate
posts.cooked:
Got “Release the Kraken!”

Standard Voss versus Haka, Absolute Zero, Fanatic, Legacy.

Voss had us on the ropes for most of the game and while the kraken was taking out a few of his minions, it was doing the bulk of its damage to Absolute Zero (or Haka and his intercession). Eventually, though, after Haka was taken out by the Kraken, the other three heroes avenged him, relentlessly pounding him with a myriad of radiant and physical damage. As he stood up and began to charge at the heroes, the kraken’s tentacles burst from the floor and pulled Voss into the dark waters.

Had the Kraken not gotten him, the Mystical Defenses certainly would have.

Also, on a related note, should there be an achievement for letting Dawn destroy herself during an eclipse? We had the fortune of her drawing that card when her health was 2.

Just got Fight The Break Of Dawn!

Citizen Dawn in Megalopolis vs Absolute Zero, Visionary, Wraith, and Fanatic. Visionary and Wraith worked together to keep the Dawn’s Auroras at the bottom of her deck and her Return from the Dawns on top such that her trash never had more than 3 citizens in it. Once Assault and Battery were chastised by Fanatic, it was all over as AZ kept healing himself, Visionary caused hemorrhaging, Wraith threw bundles of wraithmarangs and stun bolts, and Fanatic swung Absolution around to keep a Zealous Offense up. It was a Wrathful Retribution that finally caused Dawn to fall, without her merging with the power of the sun, she could not withstand the onslaught that the heroes could produce.

Did I mention I love this game?

posts.name: Matchstickman
posts.cooked:
You can’t remove the drugs from play by any means once they enter, they are indestructible.

Indestructible: If a card is indestructible, it cannot be destroyed or removed from play. If a target is indestructible, it stays inplay even if it reduced to 0 or fewer HP.

And hitting those girls into the stratosphere, nice tactic, horrible visual!

Er… thinking about it stratosphere-ing those lost girls is not as ‘game breaking’ as I had first thought, Spite plays two cards per turn so it would only delay him slightly. I guess having Wraith go before Tempest would mean you could Infrared Eyepiece the deck to your advantage and then Stratosphere the Lost Girl later in the same round to manage the stall tactic better.

posts.cooked:
Down But Not Out
Me and a friend actually got this one once before, but the other night, I got the ultimate version of this one. I was playing against Dawn with Young Legacy, Unity, Wraith, and Haka, in the Tomb of Anubis. I wasn’t trying for any achievements, but I hoped to pull off the “put all the citizens under savage mana” trick. Dawn aurora-ed the round that Haka put out Savage Mana, so that never happened. The game got brutal fast, but I ended up in a weird situation where everyone was at 1 hp, Smoke Bombs were out, and Young Legacy had Fortitude. I can’t go into details, but the tomb had 2 cards out dealing area damage, but Wraith got out 2 Mega Computers to neutralize those, and then with constantly redirecting damage from lowest to Young Legacy, I could handle anything at 2 damage or less. Dawn was only doing 2, and none of her minions that did more than 2 came out. At the end, I won just like that. Everyone was at 1. It was kinda cool.

posts.cooked:
Late to the party and very new here, but tonight we beat Omnitron for the first time - which completes my opening tour of the core set villains for “Stop, Evildoer!”, and we beat him at Wagner Mars Base, which also completes our tour of the environments.
This was also the first proper four-player game I’d played. Previously it’d just been me and my wife playing two heroes each, but tonight two of our friends came over. My wife laid first dibs on Wraith, as usual, and our friend Michael picked Ra pretty quickly. He wasn’t entirely sure how he’d cope with being an all-out offensive player, and when I described a few of the others he said he’d probably pick Haka next time. Our other friend Tam chose The Visionary and I rounded out the team with Legacy. It was a long game since we had to explain a fair few of the game mechanics, but the two who were new to the game loved it and we all had a pretty awesome time. Plus nobody dropped below 18hp the whole game. We were a healthy bunch.

posts.name: pcgamerpirate
posts.cooked:
Every...story...challenge...complete.

Our last two were Field Medic and Deus Ex Machinasaurus.

Knowing that you need phosphoresent chambers AND Tempest AND Fanatic to get Field Medic, we ended up using Rook City Wraith to help us get phosphoresent chambers at the right time and Visionary to try to get tempest's cleansing downpours. Once the chambers were in play, fanatic emboldened Tempest, who played his second cleansing downpour and used both to heal a hurt Rook City wraith for 6 HP in one turn. Then we beat Baron Blade into a pulp.

 

The Deus Ex Machinasaurus was to have Visionary ride the T-Rex with Wrest the mind. We spent the whole game trying to get the T-Rex out and it was only after Haka sacrificed himself in a lava flow that the T-Rex finally came out when we were ready, with all heroes at less than 10 HP. Unfortunately, Blade was not second highest HP on the board and Visionary hadn't had time to wrest the mind. Luckily, however, Tachyon was second highest and Tachyon had played synaptic interruption...she dodged out of the way of the rampaging T-rex who instead made a tasty meal of the Baron's battle suit.
